data.title: Proteomic analysis of SKOV3 cells expressing wild-type and mutant IGF2BP2-TurboID
data.projectDescription: Proteomic dataset identifying IGF2BP2-associated proteins in SKOV3 cells using a TurboID-based proximity labeling approach. Wild-type and mutant IGF2BP2-TurboID constructs were compared to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which IGF2BP2 regulates mRNA translation.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: SKOV3 cells expressing wild-type or mutant IGF2BP2-TurboID were incubated with 500 µM biotin for 15 minutes at 37 °C. After biotinylation, cells were chilled on ice, washed with cold PBS, and lysed in RIPA buffer containing protease inhibitors. Clarified lysates were collected, and a small aliquot was reserved as input. The remaining supernatant was incubated with streptavidin magnetic beads overnight at 4 °C. Beads were sequentially washed with RIPA buffer, 1 mM KCl, 10 mM urea, and RIPA buffer again, then eluted by boiling in 5× SDS sample buffer at 95 °C for 10 minutes. The eluates were collected for Western blotting and LC–MS/MS analysis.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: Protein identification was performed using UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot (reviewed) as the primary database, supplemented with UniProtKB/TrEMBL, NCBI RefSeq, Ensembl, or custom databases for novel sequences, isoforms, or variants. MS data were searched with Trypsin, allowing up to 2 missed cleavages, peptide mass tolerance of 20 ppm, fragment mass tolerance of 20 ppm, and minimum peptide length of 7. Carbamidomethyl (C) was set as a fixed modification; Oxidation (M), Gln→pyro-Glu (N-terminal Q), and Deamidation (N/Q) as variable modifications. PSM-level and protein-level FDR were both ≤1%. Peptide peak areas were extracted using in-house software, and iBAQ values were calculated as the total peak area of each protein group divided by the number of theoretically observable peptides. All raw MS files, search results, and iBAQ quantification tables are provided to ensure reproducibility.
